notes: Identity assessment: canonical text names Sympathy and callousness: The impact of deliberative thought on donations to identifiable and statistical victims; Deborah A. Small, George Loewenstein, Paul Slovic; Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes 102 (2007) 143–153; DOI 10.1016/j.obhdp.2006.01.005. This is a full primary article text with Studies 1–4, discussion, appendices and references, not an abstract or secondary report. No PDF was supplied, so no rendered-layout inspection was available. Assigned fields only: n_o and es_value_o. Other fields and replication are unassigned placeholders. Target ambiguity: description gives analytical thinking about identifiable-victim donations, while Study 1 Results on the located page reports multiple relevant tests. Candidates are intervention main effect F(1,115)=4.15, p<.05; identifiability-by-intervention interaction F(1,115)=5.32, p<.05; post-hoc contrast of identifiable/no-intervention against the other three cells t(117), magnitude 4.06, p<.001 (canonical text has a control character before 4.06, so sign is not independently resolved); and ordered-probit interaction X2(1)=4.72, p<.03. These candidates are not a uniquely identified simple identifiable-victim intervention contrast. No candidate was selected using numeric matching or row order. The supplied locator does not establish which test is assigned. N=121 refers to individuals approached. It is not promoted to target analytic N. No analytic N was derived from degrees of freedom, and no explicit final cell counts were supplied for summation. Candidate p bounds are retained only in notes/evidence; p_o is unassigned.
